note: Which TypeSpec/TCGC/emitter feature would remove each pattern, and whether it exists today. Drafted from an AI mapping of pattern descriptions and samples to the TCGC docs (October 2026); judgments, not verified per instance. Edit by pull request. coverage: exists (decorators exist, specs do not use them), partial (exists but misses cases), gap (new feature needed), spec-fix, not-generator. languages: per-language generator support (guidelines/capabilities.md), drafted October 2026 from TCGC docs and emitter tests; for language owners to review.

NG.name: Not generator work (handwritten runtime behavior)

override.name: @override + replaceParameter/removeParameter/addParameter/reorderParameters

P_backCompat.name: Back-compat surface from the previous GA (obsolete shims, legacy overloads, renamed members)
P_backCompat.what: Let a spec (or an API baseline file) mark removed/renamed members, overloads and enum values to be emitted as obsolete forwarding shims, including prior-version overloads when an optional parameter is added.
P_backCompat.whyShort: rename/reshape replaces the old surface; nothing keeps the old name or signature alongside as obsolete

python.note: Language-neutral back-compat; nothing in TCGC or the emitter keeps obsolete names or signatures alongside new ones.

java.note: Language-neutral back-compat; @Deprecated forwarding members are expressible but not generated.

dotnet.note: Language-neutral back-compat; [Obsolete] shims and legacy overloads are expressible but not generated from the spec.

javascript.note: Language-neutral back-compat; @deprecated aliases are expressible but not generated.

go.note: Language-neutral back-compat; Deprecated forwarding functions are expressible but not generated.

P_lroPolling.name: Custom LRO polling semantics on the poller
P_lroPolling.what: Extend LRO metadata with polling strategies (poll resource until state, delete-until-gone), expose the operation id, allow a named public operation/poller type, and require continuation-token rehydration in every emitter. Overlaps the LRO-unification proposal.
P_lroPolling.whyShort: cover standard status-monitor/Operation-Location flows; cannot express state-based polling of a resource, delete-until-404, initial 200 = in progress, operation id exposure, typed operation classes or rehydration tokens consistently across emitters

python.note: Standard pollers are generated from Azure.Core LRO metadata; state-based or delete-until-gone polling, operation-id exposure and named poller types are not.

java.note: Standard SyncPoller/PollerFlux are generated; custom polling strategies, operation-id exposure and named operation types are not.

dotnet.note: Standard Operation<T> is generated; custom polling strategies, operation-id exposure and named operation classes are not.

javascript.note: Standard pollers and restorePoller are generated; custom polling strategies, operation-id exposure and named poller types are not.

go.note: Standard runtime.Poller with resume tokens is generated; custom polling strategies and operation-id exposure are not.

P_modelProjection.name: Client model projection (public model <-> wire model mapping)

P_modelProjection.whyShort: swaps the type wholesale but generates no field-by-field conversion, so the mapping code stays handwritten

python.note: No way to declare a public model mapped onto the wire model; the conversion code is expressible but not generated.

java.note: No way to declare a public model mapped onto the wire model; the conversion code is expressible but not generated.

dotnet.note: No way to declare a public model mapped onto the wire model; the conversion code is expressible but not generated.

P_audience.what: Model the bearer-token audience as a client option with known per-cloud values (public, China, US Gov) and an endpoint-derived default; emitters generate the option, the scope composition (+/.default) and audience-error guidance.
P_audience.whyShort: scopes are fixed strings in the spec/config; no client option to pick an audience or cloud, or derive it from the endpoint

python.note: An audience keyword with per-cloud values and scope composition is expressible but not generated.

java.note: An audience option on the builder is expressible but not generated.

dotnet.note: An Audience client option with known per-cloud values is expressible but not generated.

javascript.note: credential-scopes fixes scopes at generation time; an audience client option is not generated.

go.note: Audience via cloud.Configuration service entries is expressible but not generated.

dotnet.note: Alias and computed properties are expressible but not generated; @clientName only renames.

P_modelCtors.name: Model constructor overloads (per one-of variant / required-property sets)
P_modelCtors.what: Generate named constructors or factories for input models, one per union/one-of variant (URL vs bytes) or per required-property subset, including fixed-discriminator variants.

P_responseProjection.name: Response projection (unwrap envelope, headers into result, status -> value)
P_responseProjection.what: Declare that a method returns a nested property, a model built from headers+body, or a per-status value (304 -> None, 404 -> false on DELETE/GET).

dotnet.note: HEAD-as-bool is generated, but replaceResponseWithVoid/Bytes are NOT_SUPPORTED and envelope unwrapping, header projection and per-status values are not expressible.

javascript.note: HEAD-as-bool, response replacements and include-headers-in-response are supported; envelope unwrapping and per-status values are not.

go.note: Response envelopes carry headers and HEAD-as-bool and void replacement work; envelope unwrapping and per-status values are not.

P_authSchemes.name: Azure auth schemes beyond bearer/key (shared-key HMAC, challenge-based bearer, custom auth headers)
P_authSchemes.what: Named, runtime-backed auth schemes (Azure SharedKey/HMAC signing, Key Vault/ACR style challenge auth, extra subscription-key/region headers) that emitters map to the core library's policies and credential types.
P_authSchemes.closestExisting: @useAuth (TCGC only supports HttpAuth); typespec-ts custom-http-auth-header-name / custom-http-auth-shared-key-prefix
P_authSchemes.whyShort: HttpAuth cannot express HMAC request signing or WWW-Authenticate challenge flows; the TS options cover only a custom key header in one language

python.note: Shared-key signing and challenge auth policies are expressible but TCGC only models HttpAuth.

java.note: Shared-key signing and challenge auth policies are expressible but TCGC only models HttpAuth.

dotnet.note: Shared-key signing and challenge auth policies are expressible but TCGC only models HttpAuth.

go.note: Shared-key signing and challenge auth policies are expressible but TCGC only models HttpAuth.

P_armResourceModel.name: ARM resource/collection model for non-standard operations (mgmt emitters)
P_armResourceModel.what: Let a spec bind operations the mgmt emitter cannot infer to a resource or collection: extension resources at a fixed scope, per-type resources over one parameterized operation (DNS record types), collections without a list op, resources without PATCH (tag helpers via PUT), and a resource's data type; emitters then generate the resource/collection classes, accessors, enumeration, Exists/GetIfExists, tag helpers and REST-client plumbing.
P_armResourceModel.closestExisting: ARM resource decorators (@armResourceOperations, @armResourceRead/List/Action, @extensionResource, @singleton, @armResourceCheckExistence) and ARM legacy decorators (@armOperationRoute, @customAzureResource, @renamePathParameter)

P_propertyShape.name: Generated property shape (mutability, nullability, read-only collections, flattened accessors)
